import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This page is the operational **release gate checklist for v1** — what must be
green before `:3070` is trusted as production-ready, and which lanes are
knowingly excluded and why. It complements the design/strategy doc at
[`testing/index`](./index); this page is the narrower "is v1 actually
ready" verdict, produced by
`production-test-readiness-2026-07-06` (P-007).

<Aside type="caution" title="v1 scope, not v2">
Per owner decision D-001 (2026-07-06, `production-test-readiness-2026-07-06`):
**v1 explicitly excludes p2p/shared-pot/federation** — that whole testing
lane is deferred to v2. A green v1 gate verdict means "v1 is ready," not
"every test in the repo passes." The excluded lanes are itemized below with
their filed v2 de-quarantine follow-ups.
</Aside>

## 1. What must be green for a v1 release

The **green-checkpoint gate** (`apps/operator/lib/release/green-checkpoint.ts`,
driven on an hourly tick; manually fireable via `release:checkpoint-run`) is
the single verdict. It runs the full affected/nightly test surface and
applies the file-level quarantine filter (`quarantine.txt`) before deciding
green/red. A v1 release requires:

1. **The gate's own verdict is green** (`release:deploy { op: 'status' }` →
   `gate.green: true`, `consecutiveReds` resetting to 0). Never force-deploy
   past a red gate for a real release (`op: 'force'` is the audited,
   owner-gated escape hatch for the rare no-users-window case only — see
   the CLAUDE.md "gate is everyone's job" section). The moment a
   previously-green gate first goes red, `green-checkpoint.ts` fires a LIVE
   push (desktop-native + mobile, `notifyAttention`) in addition to the
   durable Attention-panel escalation — best-effort, once per hold (2026-07-09,
   `platform-ops-batch-2026-07-09` P-002); a still-red gate on later ticks
   relies on the durable escalation's rising-urgency tiers, not a repeat push.
   Since 2026-07-10 (`stale-candidate re-triage`), a red is not taken at face
   value first: because the gate always judges a *quiet* commit ≥240s old
   (never the live tip), the checkpoint re-runs the named failing files at the
   current tip and classifies the verdict — `stale-candidate` (the files now
   PASS at tip; a peer already fixed it) auto-refires the gate on the newer
   tip (bounded by `PAPERCUSP_GATE_AUTO_REFIRE_CAP`, default 2 attempts)
   instead of holding red on already-fixed work; `real-red` (the failures
   reproduce at tip) holds the gate exactly as before. Read a hung
   `consecutiveReds` count together with the verdict's `retriage.classification`
   before assuming it's a genuine break.
2. **The green pin has advanced past the release commit** —
   `deploy.greenPinSha` includes the commit you intend to ship;
   `dev:pipeline_position` confirms `committed → staging → main (gate
   green) → deployed`.
3. **`:3070` is actually running that pin** — `deploy.deployedSha ===
   deploy.greenPinSha` (or trigger `release:deploy { op: 'trigger',
   confirm: true }` to promote a green-but-stalled pin). Since 2026-07-10
   a **deploy-staleness alarm** fires (`warn` then `urgent`) when the
   deployed pin is BOTH old (`PAPERCUSP_DEPLOY_STALE_HOURS`, default 6h)
   AND far behind tip (`PAPERCUSP_DEPLOY_STALE_COMMITS`, default 20 commits)
   — a green gate that never gets promoted is otherwise silent; don't rely
   on "the gate is green" alone as proof the pin is current.
4. **Core canonical-framework suites pass** (see §2) — Vitest unit +
   integration, Playwright E2E critical-journey specs, the Cargo/Rust
   native suite (desktop shell), and the LLM scenario suite's *behavioral*
   findings (not its historical error-burst noise — see WI-3203).
5. **The artifact drill is current** — a `.deb` built from the release
   commit boots clean on a fresh VM and preserves data across an upgrade
   (see §4). Re-run this per release, not just once.
6. **No un-triaged flaky-test candidates** — `testing:flakiness` (14d
   window) returns an empty auto-quarantine candidate list, or any
   candidates are quarantined accountably with a de-quarantine follow-up
   filed (see §3).

## 2. Signal sources and what they cover

| Source | What it proves | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| Vitest unit + integration | Per-package correctness; the bulk of the suite | `npm run test:affected[:integration]`, or the gate's full nightly run |
| Playwright (`apps/operator/e2e/*.spec.ts`) | Critical user journeys inside the Tauri shell: boot, pot/harness create, work-items flow, tests tab, deploy/admin-git, chat (WI-3204 audit) | Tests tab, or `npx playwright test` |
| Cargo (`#[cfg(test)]`, desktop shell) | Rust/Tauri native suite — ~203 test fns across `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri` | Wired into `harness_shared.test_runs` (framework=`cargo`) since WI-3228/P-009; previously **zero** cargo signal existed |
| LLM scenario suite | Operator/Papercup behavioral regressions under judged conversation scenarios | `harness_shared.llm_test_runs` / `llm_test_findings` — triaged 2026-07-06 (WI-3203); see the two active findings below |
| Artifact drill | The actual shipped `.deb` boots + upgrades correctly, not just "tests pass in-tree" | Manual VM drill, see §4 |
| Backup/restore drill | A real restore recovers a populated workspace | Manual drill, see §4 |

### Known active (non-blocking) findings from the LLM scenario triage (WI-3203)

- **WI-3229** (major) — delta-merge staleness: the operator/Papercup can show
  removed rows as still-current or stale pre-update titles after a list
  delta. Filed, not yet fixed as of this checklist's writing — track before
  calling the chat/converse surface fully hardened.
- **WI-3230** (minor) — a "banned pattern" scenario assert false-positives on
  quoted/discussed forbidden terms (assert-quality bug, not a SUT
  regression).

## 3. Excluded lanes (v1 scope cut) — `quarantine.txt`

These file patterns are excluded from the v1 green-checkpoint **verdict**
(failures still run and are logged, just don't hold the gate red). Each has
a filed, owned v2 follow-up — a quarantine here is never silent:

| Pattern(s) | Lane | v2 de-quarantine follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/sync/hyperbee/**` | p2p sync/hyperbee | WI-3240 |
| `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/shared-pot-loop/**` | shared-pot loop | WI-3241 |
| `@papercusp/operator-core::lib/p2p/**`, `lib/deployment/p2p-perf-tier3/**`, `lib/**/*p2p*.test.ts`, `lib/**/*federation*.test.ts`, `lib/**/dogfood-substrate*.test.ts`, `lib/**/substrate*.test.ts` | p2p/substrate/federation (operator-core) | WI-3242 |
| `@papercusp/p2p-voice::src/**`, `@papercusp/pubsub-substrate::src/**` | generic p2p-voice / pubsub-substrate libs | WI-3243 |
| `@papercupai/operator::apps/operator/e2e/voice-mode.spec.ts` | Known-red harness limitation (NumField blur-commit + ipcFetch transport not reliably assertable headless); feature verified working via direct API | Not v2-scoped — pre-existing headless-assertion gap, see the test's own comment |

This is implemented as a **file-level** filter in
`green-checkpoint.ts` (`applyTestQuarantine` / `parseTestQuarantine`), not a
whole-workspace exclusion — `@papercusp/operator-core` still holds the gate
for every non-matching file. Encoded + tested in WI-3210/P-012 (96/96 focused
tests green).

<Aside type="note" title="Autonomous-loop lane">
The autonomous-loop lane also remains excluded per a prior owner directive
(carried forward from before this plan) — same "logged, not gating" model.
</Aside>

## 4. Manual operational drills (per release, not just once)

These prove the *shipped artifact* behaves, not just the in-tree test
suite:

- **Artifact fresh-install + upgrade (WI-3208)**: build the `.deb`, install
  on a clean VM (pot auto-wire disabled — p2p is v2, don't join production
  swarm topics from a test frame, cf WI-1423), verify cold first-boot green
  (embedded PG boots, all migrations apply from empty, sidecar + webview up,
  no STARTUP VALIDATION errors), then install over a populated data dir and
  verify migrations apply and data survives. Last run: `.deb` sha256
  `1213d1ba0d2556b0bea70fc43107c2c55d0ad045c06c5d7f5b9ff93749c0f2ed`; 403
  migrations through 525; papercup row preserved across reinstall.
- **Backup/restore round-trip (WI-3207)**: snapshot a populated workspace
  (kopia), restore into a clean environment, boot, verify plans/work-items/
  settings intact. Last run: staging snapshot `53191` / kopia
  `57da08e7ced063167af3f591d6469455e...`; strict temp-DB restore/import
  checklist passed; fixes committed in `7ee61c4e5a62`.
  **Re-run 2026-07-17**: `papercusp-workspace` pre-deploy snapshot / kopia
  `ac6b94a7e151bf36ca0a5b7d87e9f156`; restore-to-clone (`backup:restore`)
  passed non-destructively. The temp-DB **import** step hit two real gaps —
  tracked as EI-13868 and **fixed 2026-07-19**: (1) PG18's
  `\restrict`/`\unrestrict` dump wrapper desyncs psql's COPY parser
  partway through and eventually OOMs; (2) `harness_admin` lacks
  `CREATE EXTENSION` so every `vector`-typed table (work_items, plans,
  features, escalations, …) fails to create; (3) the dump only requested
  the `vector` extension (`-e vector`), so the trigram GIN index
  (`594-memory-canonical-trgm-lexical.sql`) failed to create post-restore
  (`gin_trgm_ops does not exist`) since `pg_trgm` was never in the dump.
  **Fix**: `packages/backup/src/hook.ts` now dumps `pg_trgm` and
  `pgcrypto` alongside `vector` (fixes #3 at the source); a new helper,
  `packages/backup/scripts/restore-pg-dump.sh <dump> <target-db>
  [target-url]`, automates the import side — strips the `\restrict`/
  `\unrestrict` markers (safe for our own self-generated, trusted dump)
  and runs the import as a superuser (fixes #1/#2), creating a fresh
  scratch DB rather than touching anything live. Verified 2026-07-19: a
  restore of a freshly-generated dump (with the `pg_trgm`/`pgcrypto` fix)
  via the new script imported with **zero** `gin_trgm_ops` errors, and
  row counts for work_items/harness_plans/engineer_issues matched live
  within normal drift under active fleet load. Use the script for every
  future restore drill instead of hand-rolled `sed`/`sudo` steps.
- **Perf/stability soak (P-010, WI-3209 — in progress as of this
  checklist)**: a bounded (>=2h) soak under agent load asserting on
  `loop_lag_p95_ms` / `rss_mb` ledger columns for RSS growth + event-loop-lag
  thresholds, plus a cold-boot-time assertion. **Not yet complete** — the
  perf-field producers are fixed and live-smoked, but the full >=2h window
  had not finished collecting as of this writing. Do not treat a release as
  fully soak-verified until WI-3209 passes.

## 5. Before you cut a release — the actual sequence

1. `release:deploy { op: 'status' }` — read the gate + deploy state fresh.
   If red, fix the reds (even out of your lane) or quarantine accountably;
   never force past a red gate for a real release.
2. If gate is green but stalled, `release:deploy { op: 'trigger', confirm:
   true }` to promote it.
3. Confirm `deploy.deployedSha === deploy.greenPinSha` and that pin is at or
   after your release commit.
4. Re-run the artifact drill (§4) against the release commit if it's been
   more than a few days since the last drill — a green gate doesn't
   substitute for a fresh install/upgrade proof.
5. Check `testing:flakiness` for new auto-quarantine candidates since the
   last release; triage per §1.9 of [`testing/index`](./index).
6. Cut the release. Record the gate SHA, deploy SHA, and drill evidence on
   the release work-item/plan for the audit trail.
